## Heartburn Pattern and Likely Triggers

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

This sounds most consistent with **mild reflux/heartburn** that is being nudged by dinner habits and possibly **ibuprofen** use. The fact that it is **after dinner**, lasts **3 weeks**, and there is **no chest pain, vomiting, or weight loss** makes a non-prescription first step reasonable.

## What Is Most Likely Causing It

| Likely trigger | Why it matters | Practical change |
|---|---|---|
| Large or late dinners | A full stomach increases reflux | Eat smaller portions; finish dinner 2–3 hours before lying down |
| Fatty, fried, or spicy foods | Can relax the valve between stomach and esophagus | Reduce these for a week and compare symptoms |
| Coffee, tea, chocolate, peppermint, alcohol | Common reflux triggers in some people | Temporarily cut back or remove one at a time |
| Carbonated drinks | Can increase pressure and belching | Swap for still water |
| Ibuprofen twice weekly | NSAIDs can irritate the stomach lining and worsen heartburn | Use the lowest effective dose, take with food, and avoid extra NSAIDs if possible |
| Bending or lying down after dinner | Makes reflux more likely | Stay upright after meals; avoid tight waistbands |

## 7-Day Symptom-Tracking Plan

Track the same few items each day so patterns become obvious.

| Day | What to record | What to try |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Dinner time, portion size, heartburn timing, ibuprofen use | Eat a smaller dinner; stay upright 3 hours after eating |
| Day 2 | Foods/drinks at dinner; symptom severity 0–10 | Remove one common trigger, such as spicy or fried foods |
| Day 3 | Whether symptoms happen on a normal workday vs. stressful day | Eat slowly; avoid rushing dinner |
| Day 4 | Any late snacks or dessert | Skip food after dinner; choose water instead of soda |
| Day 5 | Sleep position and bedtime | Raise the head of the bed slightly or use a wedge pillow |
| Day 6 | Ibuprofen timing and whether it was taken with food | If needed, take only with a meal and avoid taking it near bedtime |
| Day 7 | Compare the week: frequency, severity, and strongest trigger | Decide which 1–2 changes helped most and keep them going |

### Simple tracking notes
- Rate heartburn: **0 = none, 10 = worst**
- Record: **time started, what you ate, posture, and ibuprofen use**
- Look for patterns such as: **late dinner + fried food + lying down**

## When to See a Doctor Soon

Seek medical care soon if any of these happen:

- Heartburn is **persisting beyond 2–4 weeks** despite lifestyle changes
- Symptoms are **getting more frequent or more severe**
- You develop **trouble swallowing** or food feels stuck
- You have **vomiting**, especially repeated vomiting
- You notice **black stools** or **blood in vomit**
- You have **unintentional weight loss**
- You develop **chest pain**, pressure, shortness of breath, sweating, or pain spreading to the arm/jaw
- You need **ibuprofen more often** or have stomach pain after taking it
